Hi Sarah — copying technical details below and a short recommendation.

Definitions: we typically measure latency at two points:
- edge-first-byte: time from client request hitting our edge to first byte returned (includes network to edge)
- runtime-p95: time spent in the model runtime to generate tokens (model + KV cache + decoding).
For contractual SLOs we recommend defining both: client-observed (edge) and service-side (runtime) so you can isolate network vs compute causes.

Feasibility/estimates (based on your numbers + our PoC runs):
- For <=128 token prompts on a 8-bit quantized 30B model variant on DGX A100-style nodes with our continuous-batching setup, runtime-p95 ~ 45-70ms in-region. Edge-first-byte adds ~20-40ms depending on region/network. That gives an end-to-end P95 of ~70-110ms for US/EU in typical networks.
- APAC: expected additional network delta ~80-120ms to nearest region; with APAC-local hosts (Private or Dedicated in APAC regions) we can expect similar runtime numbers as US/EU but you must provision Dedicated capacity (we can include in the proposal).
- P99: expect ~2.5x P95 in burst without extra headroom; with the autoscale/burst config we recommend (additional reserved nodes + queue shedding policies) we can keep P99 < 500ms under 2x steady burst.

Streaming specifics:
- Streaming first-byte (server-side) for typed tokens is typically <30ms from the runtime when using our streaming API. End-to-end <50ms is achievable if the client to edge network is low-latency; we saw ~40ms E2E in US PoC tests.
- For 50 concurrent streaming sessions, a single mid-size cluster (6-8 GPUs) should be sufficient for your baseline throughput; plan for 2 clusters for HA across regions.

Regional routing & data residency:
- We can enforce routing by geo-IP and client region headers. EU traffic can be pinned to EU-only runtime + storage for logs. We provide audited log retention options and can sign contractual data residency terms for EU.
- APAC residency: available via Dedicated or Private deployments in APAC regions; for pilot, routing-only with log replication controls is possible but not compliant with strict APAC residency requirements.

Recommended next steps (technical):
- We’ll produce a short SLO appendix that defines measurement points (edge vs runtime), exact metrics (P50/P95/P99), and acceptable error/backoff behavior.
- Proposed capacity plan: per-region GPU counts and autoscale policy.
- Action: Marissa/Neha will put pricing + committed capacity options into the commercial proposal.

I attached a sample SLO appendix and the raw latency test CSV from our PoC so you can inspect the distributions. Happy to jump on a 30-min tech session with your infra folks.

Thanks,
